title: Logarithmic Gaussian tail identity
statement: Let $\Phi$ be the standard Gaussian cumulative distribution function, $\varphi(t)=e^{-t^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, $R(t)=\Phi(t)(-t)/\varphi(t)$, and $L(t)=2\log(1/\Phi(t))$. For every $t<0$, with natural logarithms, $L(t)=-2\log R(t)+2\log(-t)+2\log\sqrt{2\pi}+t^2$.
replaced:
Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}\varphi(x)\,dx$, $R(t)=\Phi(t)(-t)/\varphi(t)$, and $L(t)=2\log(1/\Phi(t))$. For every real $t<0$, with natural logarithms, one has
\[
L(t)=\bigl(-2\log R(t)+2\log(-t)+2\log\sqrt{2\pi}\bigr)+t^2.
\]
